question: Which of the following is NOT an example of refraction of light?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Red colour of setting sun.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon of** refraction of light** is the shift in the path of light as it travels from one medium to another.
 
• Red colour of setting sun__:
 __
 
• It is ​due to a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.
 
• The Sun is very low in the sky at sunrise and sunset.
 
• Because of its short wavelength, blue light is dispersed more forcefully by the atmosphere, and it tends to be scattered numerous times and redirected away in various directions before reaching us.
 
• We perceive the longer wavelength yellow and red light as the sunshine travels a larger distance.
 
• As a result, the sky appears to be red in colour.
 
 
 
• A pencil submerged in a glass of water **appears bent **at the **water-air interface**, for example.
 
• The ray of light **bends towards normal **as it moves from a **rarer to a denser medium**, and **away from normal** as it moves from a **denser to a rarer** medium.
 
• **Lenses, magnifying glasses, prisms, and rainbows **are all possible because of this bending through refraction.
 
• **Laws of Refraction: **
 
 
• The incident ray, the refracted ray, and the normal at the point of incidence, all lie in the same plane.
 
• The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence and sine of the angle of refraction is constant.
 
 
 
• The ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the second medium of greater density is used to determine the Refractive Index. 
 
 
• The higher the refractive index, the slower light travels, causing a proportionately greater change in light direction within the material.
 
 
 
• The **velocity of light c** of a particular wavelength in empty space divided by its** velocity v** in a substance, or **n = c/v**, is also known as the** refractive index.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Image formation by the human eye__:**

 __
 
• The** majority of refraction** in the eye occurs when light rays pass through the **eye's curved, front surface** (cornea).
 
• Light rays **converge** most at the cornea and when entering and exiting the lens, forming a** picture **on the retina.
 
• Rays from the object's top and bottom are traced, resulting in an** inverted actual image** on the retina.
 
 
 
• **Formation of the rainbow__:**
 __
 
• Rainbows are created when sunlight is scattered by water droplets (such as raindrops or fog) in a process known as **refraction.**
 
• When sunlight passes through a **medium denser than air**, such as a** raindrop**, it refracts, changing its direction.
 
• When light enters the raindrop, it is** refracted, reflected off the back**, and then** refracted again** as it escapes and travels to our eyes.
 
 
 
• **Twinkling of stars__:**​
 
 
• The twinkling of a star is caused by starlight being **refracted** by the atmosphere.
 
• When starlight enters the earth's atmosphere, it undergoes** constant refraction** before reaching the surface.
 
• Atmospheric refraction takes place in a material with a** fluctuating refractive index.**
 
• The apparent location of the star differs significantly from its real position due to the **atmosphere's bending** of starlight **towards the normal.**
 
• When viewed near the horizon, the star appears slightly **higher **(above) than its real position.
 
• Because the stars are so far away, they resemble **point sources of light.**
 
• The** apparent position **of the star changes throughout time, as does the amount of starlight that enters the eye.
 
• The star flickers, seeming brighter and fainter at different periods, causing the** twinkling effect.**
